drawn:
I built option D, "Split and play": C's split bookmark with h1's tail cut. Two straight cuts of the same width; the halves make a pause and the left tail makes a play. Every file is in place, the master is inside the safe circle (reach 32.56 of 33), and the build reproduces every file exactly. I'd show it to Richard because he asked for this combination and it is drawn as well as I can draw it, but I rank it just under C and A.

**self_score: 6.5**

**Master (108 dp canvas)**
- **Bookmark:** the shared one (43.5 dp wide, top 27.1), with C's 6.21 dp slot (1/7 of the width). The right half is C's path exactly: the build takes it from C's build.
- **Diagonal cut:** it follows the notch's right edge carried on to the left edge at y 52.69. It is 6.21 dp wide measured square to itself (7.40 dp down the left edge), exactly the slot's width. The upper-left piece's bottom edge and the right half's foot are one straight line, broken only by the slot.
- **Play:** 20.75 × 16.03 dp. Depth = height × 17/22, the same shape as A's and B's play at 0.74 of A's size. It is 9.8% of the paper.
- **Tip gap:** the rounded tip stops 4.23 dp short of the slot's line (2.61 from the sharp point). On a 1× home screen that is 2.8 px, and the three pixel columns before the slot are clear (the nearest is 5% paper).
- **Other spacing:** 6.21 dp between the upper piece and the play, 10.7 dp from the play to the right half.
- **Ink:** 31.2% of the tile (C 34). The centroid sits 1.1 dp right of centre, because both cuts take paper from the left half.
- **Corners:** C's rule. Two shoulders at 5.12 dp; all nine corners the cuts make at 1.92 dp. Pixel cuts have sharp cut corners.

**Diagonal width, decided by looking**
- I drew it at 0.75, 1, 1.15 and 1.3 times the slot. At 0.75 it reads as a crack and the play's tip crowds the slot. At 1.15 and 1.3 it looks heavier than the slot and the play shrinks away from the gap. At exactly 1 they read as two cuts made with the same blade.
- One slot is also the narrowest width that keeps three clear columns at 1×. At 0.95 the nearest column is already 22% paper.
- I measured the gap as clear pixel columns (under the sheet's 12% "touched" threshold), and give the sharp-tip distance alongside.

**Small sizes**

| Size | What I drew | Gap before the slot | Soft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 48 px | C's 28 × 34 bookmark, 4 px slot and right half; diagonal ends on (10, 23) and (10, 29); play 12 × 9.33 px | sharp 2.67 px; 3 clear columns (nearest 4%) | 6.1% (C 3.3, h1 5.1) |
| 32 px | C's 21 × 24 bookmark and 3 px slot; slope 2/3; play 10 × 7.5 px | sharp 1.5 px; 2 clear columns (nearest 8%) | 7.9% (C 5.7) |
| 16 px | C's cut, byte for byte apart from its comment | no play | 2.4% |
| Glyph | base's plain bookmark | no play | 6.3% |

- **48 px:** I used a 6 px vertical drop rather than 5. A 5 px drop is the slot's width (4.2 px square) but leaves only two clear columns before the slot. So at 48 px the diagonal is about a pixel wider than the slot (5.05 px square against 4).
- **32 px:** I changed the notch slope from C's 0.65 to 2/3, h1's slope at this size. On 0.65 the diagonal meets the left edge at y 14.35 and its stairs start unevenly. On 2/3 every end lands on a whole pixel and the stairs step evenly. A 4 px drop makes the diagonal 3.33 px wide, the slot's width to a third of a pixel. A 5 px drop gives a 2.25 px sharp gap but a visibly heavier diagonal.
- **16 px:** I chose C's split alone. A 6/4/2 whole-pixel play does fit, 1 px from the slot. At real size, though, the stair and the slot join into one bent dark line, the left half breaks into two pieces, and the play reads as a nick in the bar.
- **Glyph:** plain bookmark, on the same evidence as C. Drawn as D, it sits beside the clock as a play-and-pause sign, and on the media card it repeats the real button in both states. `media-card.png` shows this, and `media-card.mjs` rebuilds it (C's mock could not be rebuilt from the repo).

**What still bothers me**
1. Play with pause is the media toggle. It reads most like a player control in the light colourway, where three ink pieces stand on paper.
2. Some of the old slash survives: the long top-left to bottom-right line, though the slot now breaks it.
3. The 32 px sharp tip is only 1.5 px from the slot, so it meets the 2 px minimum only on the clear-pixel measure.
4. At 48 px the diagonal is a pixel wider than the slot.
5. D's 32 px right half ends at y 22 where C's ends at 22.15. If both options are kept, setting C's 32 px feet to its existing '2:3' option would make the two match. I didn't edit C.
6. The play is small, and it only appears from 32 px up. The favicon, the 1× toolbar and the glyph all show C.
7. The mark is three pieces, so any one-colour use (print, emboss, a sticker) has to keep both cuts open.
8. D isn't on the study page yet: `page.json` is outside my folder, so it needs adding there and `tools/build-page.mjs` re-running.

The prototype folders (`candidates/zz-d*`) are deleted, the base files are unchanged, and my scratch scripts are in the session scratchpad only.

checked:
Verdict: **pass.** D's drawing is correct and I left all five SVGs byte-identical. The defects were all in `meta.json`'s wording, plus one imprecise measurement in `build.mjs`. I fixed them all by editing `build.mjs`, then re-ran it, `sheet.mjs`, the build again, and `media-card.mjs`.

I checked the drawings with my own rasteriser, which works out each pixel's exact coverage and doesn't use D's code.

**Defects found, all fixed**
1. **`idea` was three sentences.** The brief allows one or two. I merged it into two with the same content.
2. **Wrong reason for the off-centre ink in `built`.** It said "both cuts take paper from the left half", but the slot is centred and takes from both halves equally. It now says the second cut alone shifts the centroid.
3. **"The diagonal's ends land on whole pixels" (48 px) was only half true.** Only its left-edge ends do (y 23 and 29); its slot end is at y 30.71 and the play's tip at (19.33, 35). Reworded to "meets the left edge on whole pixels".
4. **"At 24 px its play is also a 5 px sliver" was wrong.** The play in the glyph study is 7 × 5.6 px. The text is now computed from a new `GLYPH_STUDY` constant in `build.mjs`, which `media-card.mjs` also uses so the two can't drift. `media-card.png` re-rendered byte-identical.
5. **The 1× faint pixel was quoted as 5%; it is really 4.2%.** The build's 16 × 16 supersampling overstated it. At 32 × 32 the build matches my exact figures: 4% at 1×, 4% at 48 px, 8% at 32 px and 22% at 0.95 of the slot.
6. **The half-pixel offset wasn't mentioned.** The 32 and 16 px marks sit half a pixel left of the tile's centre, inherited from C; C's meta says so and D's didn't. Added.

**What passed**
- **Files:** all six exist with the right viewBoxes. They use only svg, rect and path with fills, and no stroke, mask, clip path, filter, gradient or opacity. Colours are exactly #F3F2EE and #111112, and #FFFFFF in the glyph. Each cut opens with `geom.tileRect(N)`.
- **Silhouette:**
  - The master's bounding box and reach (32.56) equal the base's, and no point of D lies outside the base bookmark.
  - At 48, 32 and 16 px no pixel of D has more paper than C's cut at that size.
  - The 16 px cut and the glyph are C's apart from the comment.
  - At 32 px the notch slope is 2/3 where C's is 0.65 (at most 0.15 px), and `meta.json` gives the reason.
- **Geometry:**
  - The slot is C's: 6.214 dp, 1/7 of the width.
  - The diagonal's slope is 11/17 and it lies on the line through the right tip and the apex (off by less than 0.001 dp).
  - The play's top edge runs parallel to the right flank, 6.214 dp from the diagonal measured square (7.401 dp vertically), which is the slot's width. Its bottom edge lies on the notch's left flank.
  - Depth is 16.03 = 20.75 × 17/22.
  - Gaps: 6.21 dp from the upper piece to the play and 10.70 dp from the play to the right half, as claimed.
  - At 48 px the diagonal is 5.05 px wide and the play 12 × 9.33 px; at 32 px the diagonal is 3.33 px and the play 10 × 7.5 px.
  - Corner rule: of 11 corners, the two shoulders are at 5.118 dp and the nine cut corners at 1.919 dp. In the pixel cuts only the shoulders are rounded.
- **Pixels:**
  - Straight edges sit on whole pixels.
  - The pieces stay separate even at a 0.5% coverage threshold: three at 48 px, 32 px, 1×, 64 px and 4×, and two at 16 px. Nothing touches corner to corner.
  - The slot (4, 3 and 1 px) and the diagonal (5.05 and 3.33 px) meet each size's minimum.
  - The glyph sits inside its padding (x 4–20, y 2–22).
  - Softness, D against C against the base:

| Size | D | C | Base |
|---|---|---|---|
| 48 px | 6.1% | 3.3% | 3.3% |
| 32 px | 7.9% | 5.7% | 5.2% |
| 16 px | 2.4% | 2.4% | 10.9% |
| Glyph | 6.3% | 6.3% | 6.3% |

  D is higher at 48 and 32 px because it has more diagonals; `meta.json` says so.
- **Looks:** at 8×, 4× and 1× (dark, light and themed) the diagonal and slot look even and nothing is crowded. The outline is centred and the ink sits 1.1 dp right, which is stated.
- **Words:** `one` is 78 characters, spelling is British, and I found no inverted-emphasis constructions.

**What remains (not changed)**
- **The play's tip passes the minimum only in rendered pixels.** Its distance to the slot's line is 2.82 px at 1× (minimum 3), 2.67 px at 48 px (3) and 1.5 px at 32 px (2). In pixels there are 3, 3 and 2 clear columns, the nearest holding 4.2%, 3.6% and 8.3% paper, and no paper lies across that gap. Closing it means widening the diagonal; at 32 px that makes it 4.16 px against the 3 px slot, which looked heavier when I rendered it and breaks the designer's same-width decision. `meta.json` states both measures.
- **At 48 px the diagonal is 5.05 px against the 4 px slot.** Stated.
- **At 16 px and in the glyph D is C.** On the blind sheet's toolbar rows, icons 2 and 4 are identical. Documented.
- **Running D's build rewrites base's six generated files.** `base/build.mjs` writes its files whenever it's imported, and C imports it. The bytes are identical and only the timestamps change. That file is outside D's folder, so I left it.

**Blind sheet:** rendered with six numbered icons and no names; D is number 2.

icons.sees: A white bookmark ribbon with a solid black play triangle punched into its upper half, on a black disc or tile.
icons.guess: A 'watch later' or saved-media app, like saved videos or a podcast queue.
icons.negative: No. It reads as positive: saved, plus play. One catch: on the dark wallpaper the black disc disappears completely, so it floats as a bare white shape next to coloured neighbours.

icons.sees: Two tall white bars like a pause sign. The left bar is cut short on a slant and has a small separate play arrow tucked under it. The right bar ends in a slanted point.
icons.guess: A music or podcast player, because it shows play and pause controls.
icons.negative: Partly. The two bars read as pause first, and the shortened left bar looks snapped off. It can read as paused or broken before it reads as a bookmark.

icons.sees: A plain solid white bookmark ribbon with a V-notch, on black.
icons.guess: A bookmarks, reading list or 'saved items' app. It could also be a generic save button.
icons.negative: No. It reads as neutral to positive: saved.

icons.sees: Two tall white bars with slanted bottoms that together make a bookmark split down the middle. At a glance it is a pause sign, or the numeral II.
icons.guess: A media player, or maybe a books or reading app.
icons.negative: Yes, the strongest pause read of the six, because two upright bars is the universal pause symbol. It also looks like a bookmark torn in half.

icons.sees: A white square whose bottom is cut on a diagonal from the bottom-right corner up to the left side, with a small play arrow in the cut-off corner. The black gap runs corner to corner like a slash.
icons.guess: A video, slideshow or presentation app, or perhaps a document viewer.
icons.negative: Yes. The diagonal black gap reads as a slash through a box, the usual mark for off, disabled, blocked or muted. At home-screen and toolbar size it looks like a crossed-out square.

icons.sees: A bookmark with a play triangle cut into it and a tiny pause sign (two bars) inside the triangle.
icons.guess: A podcast or audio player with a saved queue.
icons.negative: Mildly. A pause sign inside a play triangle looks like a player's play/pause button, so it can read as 'paused'. It feels like a button state rather than an app.

cold.families: There are two families and one odd one out. Whole-bookmark family: 1, 3 and 6 share the same notched ribbon outline; 1 and 6 add a play cut-out and 3 is the bare version. Split family: 4 and 2 split the ribbon into two bars, and 2 adds a play arrow under the left half. The odd one out is 5. It is the only lopsided one, with a single diagonal where the others have a V-notch, so it stops looking like a bookmark and matches none of the others. Grouped by what is drawn on them instead, 1, 2, 5 and 6 have a play mark and 3 and 4 do not. All six are flat white on black. On the dark wallpaper the tile almost vanishes, completely for 1 and 4, so they look like bare shapes beside the coloured app icons. On the light wallpaper they are the heaviest thing on the screen.
cold.smallest: At 16 px, six icons shrink to four tellable shapes. Still distinct: 3, a solid bookmark, and 5, a box with a diagonal slash (distinct, but it now clearly reads as crossed out). Same blob: 1 and 6 both become a bookmark with a dark notch, because 6's pause bars disappear. Same blob: 2 and 4 both become the same pair of bars, because 2's little play arrow is lost or looks like a chipped corner. Even 3 against 1 and 6 comes down to one dark speck. On the dark toolbar the black tiles blend into the bar, but the white shapes fall into the same groups.

ranking.why: Best. The bookmark says 'saved for later' and the play cut-out says 'listen'; both read instantly and still work at 16 px. Miss: a play triangle leans towards video or 'watch later', and nothing says article or voice.
Says the same 'save and play' as 1, but the pause bars add clutter and can read as 'paused'. At 16 px it can't be told apart from 1.
The clearest 'read later' sign and sharp at every size, but it says nothing about reading aloud. In a browser toolbar it would be mistaken for the browser's own bookmark button.
Has a bookmark hint and a play arrow, but it first reads as pause and play controls with a snapped-off left half. At 16 px it turns into 4.
The bookmark outline shows at large size, but it reads as a pause button (audio stopped) and has no 'listen' sign. When small it becomes the same as 2.

A page with a play arrow could hint 'play this page', but it looks least like a bookmark and matches none of the others. The diagonal reads as a slash (off or muted), the worst message for a read-aloud app.
